title: Denial Worksheet Rule: Units Concerned on a Denied Test-Strip Line
content:
The units concerned by a non-covered item patient charge on a denied test-strip claim of the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program are read from the denied claim's history and the shipment it bills.

**Rule.** The units concerned are, when the denied claim also carries a remittance and the denial code is CO-151, the shipment's units above the units the treatment-class allowance gives for its supply days; when the denied claim carries no remittance, every unit of the shipment; and otherwise the units the notice covers.

- The denied claim *carries a remittance* when a remittance has been posted against that claim.
- *Units above* the allowance units are the shipment's units less those allowance units, and never fewer than none.

| Remittance posted against the denied claim | Denial code | Units concerned |
|---|---|---|
| yes | CO-151 | the shipment's units above the allowance units for its supply days |
| no | any | every unit of the shipment |
| yes | any other code | the units the notice covers |

**Worked cases (hypothetical figures)**

- Customer not treated with insulin, allowance 100 strips per 90 days, shipment of 6 units for 90 days, remittance posted, CO-151: 100 times 90, divided by 90 and by 50, is 2 allowance units; the units concerned are 6 less 2, that is 4.
- The same shipment for an insulin-treated customer with an allowance of 450 strips: 9 allowance units, so no unit is above them and the units concerned are none.
- No remittance posted against the denied claim: all 6 units are concerned.
- A PR-204 denial with a remittance posted: the units the notice covers.
